construct: Pathogenic variants in genes such as AGPAT2 or BSCL2 impair adipocyte development or function and prevent normal storage of triglyceride in adipose tissue. The resulting near-total loss of body fat causes ectopic lipid deposition, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance/diabetes, and fatty liver.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Near-total absence of adipose tissue since infancy with muscular appearance, hepatomegaly, acanthosis nigricans, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperglycemia identifies congenital generalized lipodystrophy.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Glycogen storage disease type I can cause hepatomegaly and hypertriglyceridemia, but it causes fasting hypoglycemia and does not produce congenital near-total loss of subcutaneous fat. Cushing syndrome and Prader-Willi syndrome cause increased adiposity, not lipodystrophy.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The congenital generalized loss of adipose tissue is the discriminator that makes congenital generalized lipodystrophy uniquely correct despite overlap in hepatomegaly or dyslipidemia with other disorders.
